cohort: The study included 366 term singleton pregnancies (183 dinoprostone-induced labor, 183 spontaneous labor) from May 2019 to February 2021 at the Jagiellonian University Hospital.
finding: Higher pre-pregnancy BMI and excessive gestational weight gain significantly increased the risk of cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: The association between higher pre-pregnancy BMI and increased gestational weight gain with elevated cesarean delivery rates was especially prominent in dinoprostone-induced labor compared to spontaneous labor.
